task: look up a specific parameterized public fact and read off the right value: enter the identifying parameters (a place and day for a weather forecast on weather.com or accuweather, a flight number on flightaware or the airline's site, a route and time on a transit-schedule site, a team for a sports score, a channel for a TV listing), get the result for those parameters, and read the needed value; complete when the queried value for the RIGHT parameters (right city, right flight number, right date, right route) is on screen. Surface pinned: a public information site or app (weather, flight-status, transit-schedule, sports scores, TV listings). Variants: news commentary or analysis videos, storm-chasing/weather-event footage, sports highlight reels, and app "review" content do not belong.

tree.label: Look up the record

questions.say_example: It's over <place>, tracking toward <destination>.

questions.question: What is the current status of the selected plane?
questions.why: The bottom panel displayed a barometric altitude of 0 ft and a ground speed of 0 kts, indicating the plane was still on the ground.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the real-time context of whether the selected plane is currently active in the air or still on the ground.
questions.check: What altitude and ground speed does the panel show?
questions.say_example: Still on the ground - altitude and speed both read zero.

questions.question: Are you reading the requested details for Mars from the popup?
questions.why: The popup displays the exact coordinates and visibility for Mars, which is the requested information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the correct celestial object was selected and its details accurately retrieved.
questions.check: What coordinates and visibility does the popup show?
questions.say_example: Read Mars at <coordinates>, <visibility note>.

questions.question: Did you check the current altitude and speed of the aircraft in the telemetry graph?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Speed & altitude graph' showing a calibrated altitude of 42,975 ft and a ground speed of 519 kts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses out on specific real-time telemetry details of the flight, such as its exact altitude and speed.
questions.check: What altitude and ground speed does the telemetry graph show?
questions.say_example: Cruising at <altitude> doing <speed>.

questions.question: What data source and exact coordinates does the expanded position show?
questions.why: The screen contained specific tracking details like the ADS-B data source and exact latitude and longitude that needed to be read.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the precise tracking details and coordinates if the agent fails to uncover and read this information.
questions.check: What data source and coordinates does the expanded section show?
questions.say_example: Position comes from <satellite tracking>, coordinates included.

questions.question: Is the field the person asked for locked behind a paid plan?
questions.why: This matters because while basic details like flight times and route progress are visible, scrolling reveals that certain advanced fields are locked behind a paywall.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to see exactly which data points are paywalled and decide if a subscription is worth purchasing.
questions.check: Which fields are displayed, and which carry a lock, upgrade, or subscription label - and at what price?
questions.say_example: The <field> you want is behind a paid plan at <price>. The free part gives <what's free>. Pay, or make do with that?

questions.question: Should you explore the paid subscription plans to remove ads from the interface?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Remove ads' button that opened a page with annual subscription tiers ranging from $9.99 to $499.99.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether paying for an ad-free experience is worth the cost for their usage.
questions.check: What does the remove-ads page offer, and at what prices?
questions.say_example: Skipped the remove-ads pitch.

questions.question: Should you skip the additional services offered?
questions.why: The screen showed upsell options for preferred seats and prepaid baggage that are not needed to find the requested public fact.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses time or risks unintended purchases if the agent interacts with irrelevant upsell offers.
questions.check: What add-on services does the page offer?
questions.say_example: Skipped seats and bags - not what you asked for.

questions.question: Should you accept the brief flight status on the search results page, or click through to a dedicated site for more details?
questions.why: The search results provided a high-level summary of the flight's delay and terminals, but clicking a dedicated link like FlightAware offers more comprehensive tracking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide if a quick summary is sufficient or if they need to investigate deeper for live tracking details.
questions.check: What details does the summary card show, and which links does it offer?
questions.say_example: The card answered it, so I stopped there.

questions.question: Do you want to check the current location of the incoming aircraft using the 'Where is my plane right now?' button?
questions.why: The screen displays the assigned gates and offers a 'Where is my plane right now?' button to track the physical aircraft before departure.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to proactively track the incoming aircraft to anticipate any potential delays not yet reflected in the schedule.
questions.check: Does the page offer an incoming-aircraft view?
questions.say_example: Checked where your plane is coming from.

questions.question: Has the page finished loading so you can view the aircraft details?
questions.why: The screen shows a blank tab reading 'Loading...', meaning the aircraft photo and metadata are not yet visible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The ability to ensure the page has fully loaded before attempting to read and verify the requested information.
questions.check: Does the tab still show Loading?
questions.say_example: Waited for the page to finish.

questions.question: Are the playback settings correct before you start the playback?
questions.why: Clicking 'Start playback' updates the map interface to show the historical view based on the configured settings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to confirm the playback settings match their desired parameters before initiating the view.
questions.check: What date and time do the playback settings show?
questions.say_example: Set playback for <May 12, 9:40 pm>.

questions.question: When should you pause the flight playback?
questions.why: The playback control bar shows the time progressing rapidly at 12x speed, requiring you to pause at exactly 04:46 to capture the yellow aircraft's correct position.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually track the moving aircraft and precisely time the pause to capture its exact location.
questions.check: What time does the playback clock show?
questions.say_example: Paused the playback at <9:47>.

children.label: Verify the record
children.note: 7.1 or 7.2 on document-backed runs - 7.2 is the cheap form. 7.3 and 7.4 wherever two numbers claim the same fact. 7.5 and 7.6 on live surfaces. the checks share screens with 6; here the user is comparing, not collecting.

questions.question: Is the value being reported carried with the unit, timezone, and day the page actually states for it?
questions.why: Values like '08:00' or '32' are meaningless without the context of the timezone (e.g., local vs destination) or unit (Celsius vs Fahrenheit), which are often visually separated into a global header or toggle switch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user acts on a fundamentally misunderstood fact (like arriving hours late or dressing for the wrong weather) because the agent stripped the value from its visual context.
questions.check: What unit or timezone label does the page state for the value - in the header, the column, or a toggle away from the number?
questions.say_example: Lands at <6:30> - that's <Dubai> time, and it's <the next day> there.

children.label: Check the record against the source

questions.question: Does the screen show the result for the exact parameters you requested?
questions.why: Information sites sometimes default to a different date, nearby location, or similar route if the exact query isn't available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might receive incorrect information if the agent fails to verify that the displayed result matches the requested parameters.
questions.check: What identifying fields does the page display - location, date, flight, route, passenger, period - and what did the request name?
questions.say_example: The page slid to <what it shows> instead of the <thing> you asked for. Re-querying.

questions.question: Did the site display a 'Showing results for...' message indicating it auto-corrected your search parameter?
questions.why: Search engines and public info sites often silently correct typos (e.g., swapping a flight number or city name) and display a banner at the top.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might be fed data for a completely different city or flight because the agent didn't notice the silent auto-correction banner at the top of the results.
questions.check: Does the page show a 'Showing results for' or similar correction notice, and what did it change?
questions.say_example: The site quietly swapped your search to <corrected>. Putting your original back.

children.label: Check the numbers against each other

questions.question: Do the record's own numbers agree with each other?
questions.why: Checking that the elapsed time and remaining time on the progress bar add up to the total travel time confirms the flight data is consistent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the reported flight duration is mathematically consistent with the current progress.
questions.check: What do the related figures on the page each read - parts against totals, chart against legend, derived against stated, status against telemetry?
questions.say_example: The page disagrees with itself - <one number> here, <the other> there. I'll report the direct reading and flag the other.

questions.question: Based on the incoming aircraft's arrival time, is your flight likely to depart on time?
questions.why: Comparing the incoming plane's arrival time to your scheduled 7:42 PM departure reveals if there is enough of a buffer to avoid a delay.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of personally calculating the turnaround time to gauge the real likelihood of a delay.
questions.check: What arrival time does the incoming aircraft show, and what departure time does the person's flight show?
questions.say_example: Your plane lands at <7:20> and you're due out at <7:42>. That's <22 minutes> between.

questions.question: Do two screens or sources give the same fact different values?
questions.why: Google's flight status card shows a scheduled departure of 11:20, which contradicts the 11:30 AM takeoff time listed on FlightAware.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to notice the conflicting departure times and verify which schedule is actually correct.
questions.check: What value does each source or screen display for the same field?
questions.say_example: <One site> says <11:20>, <the other> says <11:30>. I'll go with <the airline's own site> and note the other.

questions.question: Did a field of the record change while it was being watched?
questions.why: The screen showed the incoming flight's destination gate had changed to S/B28, matching the departure gate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the confirmation that the incoming flight's gate now matches their departure gate.
questions.check: What does the field show now, against what it showed earlier in this run?
questions.say_example: Just changed - the gate is now <B28>.

questions.question: Should you follow the link to NOAA's NCEI for finalized data?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that the displayed data is preliminary and provides a link to access the complete, finalized climate record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether preliminary data is sufficient for their needs or if they require the official, finalized records.
questions.check: Does the page state the data is preliminary, and where does it link for the finalized record?
questions.say_example: This page calls its numbers preliminary. The final ones live at <the linked source> - want the final?

questions.question: What is the difference between the yellow and blue aircraft icons on the map?
questions.why: The screen displays both yellow and blue aircraft icons, which indicate whether the flight is being tracked by terrestrial or satellite receivers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the technical context of how the flight's location data is being sourced, which can affect the expected accuracy and update frequency of the tracking.
questions.check: What does the map legend say each icon color means?
questions.say_example: Blue means satellite tracking, per the legend.

questions.question: Is the weather forecast data current, or is it displaying an outdated timestamp?
questions.why: The screen shows an 'Updated 11/27/10 8:25AM' timestamp, indicating the weather data might be severely outdated and unreliable for current planning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives obsolete weather information because the agent failed to check the last updated timestamp.
questions.check: What updated-at timestamp or freshness label does the page show - including 'not current', 'estimated', 'delayed', or 'preliminary' markers?
questions.say_example: This reading is from <the shown date> - it's stale. Finding a fresher source.

children.label: Export the result
children.note: 8.1 then 8.2 on data runs; 8.3 where the record offers itself as a document - offered four times in this corpus, taken zero.

questions.question: Did the data file download after you clicked submit?
questions.why: Checking for the browser download notification ensures that the system finished loading and successfully delivered the CSV file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent assumes the submission worked without confirming the download, you might not actually receive the requested data file.
questions.check: Does the browser show the completed download, and what filename and size?
questions.say_example: Downloaded <the station CSV>, <2 MB>.

questions.question: Does the produced output - generated text, preview, or downloaded file - actually carry the request's parameters?
questions.why: Verifying the generated text in the 'Flight Details' area ensures that the copied report accurately reflects the specific flight parameters you just input.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to double-check that the generated flight details string contains the correct information before it is copied.
questions.check: What identifiers do the output's own header or body show, against the parameters that were entered?
questions.say_example: The file that came back is for <what its header says>, not your <request>. Re-running it.

questions.question: Which downloaded file should you open to view the requested data?
questions.why: The browser download popup shows multiple downloaded files with different formats, so you must select the correct one to find the specific fact.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose which specific file format to open and inspect for the requested information.
questions.check: Which files does the download list show?
questions.say_example: Opened <the station CSV>.

questions.question: Are all the files downloaded and in the folder?
questions.why: The screen shows the downloaded files in the folder, including their types and sizes, confirming the data retrieval.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the correct data files were successfully downloaded and are ready for use.
questions.check: Which files does the folder show, with what types and sizes?
questions.say_example: All <4> files are in the folder.

questions.question: Does the pasted record go in the row directly after the last filled one, rather than leaving blank rows in the sheet?
questions.why: The spreadsheet showed the last populated row was 130, meaning pasting into row 136 leaves several empty rows in the dataset.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure new records are added contiguously without creating unexplained gaps in their tracking sheet.
questions.check: What is the last populated row shown in the sheet?
questions.say_example: Added it at row <131>, right under the last entry.

questions.question: Ready to send the itinerary to this address?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Share itinerary' section with an email field and a 'Send' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the convenience of having the retrieved itinerary automatically forwarded to your email address.
questions.check: What email address is entered in the share field?
questions.say_example: Ready to send the itinerary to <address>. Send it, or change the address?

children.label: Keep watching the target
children.note: 9.1 for a server-side alert; 9.2 and 9.3 for a hand-built dashboard; 9.4 to keep the query itself. each turns a one-off lookup into a standing view - nothing else in the corpus persists past the tab.

children.label: Set up a standing alert
children.note: 9.1.1 to 9.1.4 in the wizard's own numbered order, with try-then-revert exploration inside nearly every section; then 9.1.5.

questions.question: Do you need to use the advanced options to filter the flight by origin, destination, or aircraft type?
questions.why: The screen provides an advanced options checkbox that reveals fields for origin, destination, and aircraft type, which might be necessary if the flight number alone applies to multiple routes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the exact flight leg is selected if the agent skips these filters when the flight number alone is ambiguous.
questions.check: Does the form offer advanced filter fields, and what do they contain?
questions.say_example: Narrowed the alert to your route.

questions.question: Should I set up an alert for this flight?
questions.why: The flight tracking page displays an 'Alert Me' button alongside the current flight details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to receive automated, proactive notifications about changes to the flight's status.
questions.check: Does the page show an alert option for this flight?
questions.say_example: There's an Alert Me option if you ever want ongoing updates.

questions.question: What duration should the flight alert be active for?
questions.why: The screen offers 'Single Day', 'Multiple Days', and 'Indefinite' options for the alert duration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify how long they want to receive flight alerts.
questions.check: Which duration options does the form list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Alert set for <the single day>.

questions.question: Which specific date should you set the single-day alert for?
questions.why: The screen showed a calendar widget requiring a specific day to be selected for the alert.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the exact date for the alert, potentially resulting in receiving information for the wrong day.
questions.check: What date is selected on the alert calendar?
questions.say_example: Watching <March 8>.

questions.question: Which specific flight route should trigger the alert?
questions.why: The screen offered a choice between specific flight routes like 'Dallas Love Field ► [name]' or 'All', so the correct route must be selected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The person loses the ability to specify the exact flight route for the alert, which could result in receiving irrelevant notifications.
questions.check: Which route options does the form list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Alert tied to <the route>, not all of them.

questions.question: What relationship to the flight should you select for the alert recipient?
questions.why: The screen provided a dropdown next to the email address to specify the recipient's role, such as 'On the Flight', for receiving flight alerts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately specify their relationship to the flight when setting up the alert.
questions.check: Which relationship options does the dropdown list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Marked you as <on the flight>.

questions.question: Do you want to customize the specific events that trigger alerts?
questions.why: The screen displayed an 'Advanced Options' dropdown with checkboxes for specific flight events like 'Scheduled', 'Departure', and 'Cancelled'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control exactly which flight status updates they receive notifications for.
questions.check: Which event checkboxes does the form show, and which are ticked?
questions.say_example: It'll fire on <delays and cancellations>.

questions.question: Should I configure social media or mobile alerts for this flight?
questions.why: The screen offers checkboxes to send flight alerts to mobile email, Twitter, or Facebook.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to receive automated flight updates on their preferred social media or mobile platforms.
questions.check: Which channels does the form offer, and which are enabled?
questions.say_example: Email only - left the social hookups off.

questions.question: What information will the alert email contain?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Preview Sample' popup showing the exact flight arrival details, terminal, and gate information that would be sent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify exactly what flight details and links will be sent to the recipient before setting up the alert.
questions.check: What does the preview popup show the alert will include?
questions.say_example: The alert mails you <gate, terminal, and times>.

questions.question: What does the alert cover, and to whom does it go?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Success' modal stating the alert was successfully created, which must be dismissed to proceed to the tracking page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the explicit confirmation that their alert configuration was actually saved by the system.
questions.check: Does the page show a success message for the alert, and what does it cover?
questions.say_example: The alert's on - you'll get an email at <address> if <the flight> changes.

questions.question: Does the quota count match the recipients you set up?
questions.why: The dashboard shows two distinct notification recipients for the same flight but lists only one alert as enabled, confirming that multiple recipients count as a single alert against your quota.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might misinterpret the quota summary and incorrectly assume only one recipient was successfully configured, leading to unnecessary troubleshooting or missed notifications.
questions.check: How many alerts does the dashboard list as enabled, and how many recipients?
questions.say_example: Both addresses ride on one alert - <1> of <your quota> used.

questions.question: Do you want to delete any of the saved cities?
questions.why: The screen shows a list of saved cities like Palm Springs and Las Vegas with an option to delete them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manage and clean up their list of saved locations.
questions.check: Which saved cities does the list show?
questions.say_example: Left your saved cities alone.

questions.question: What city do you want to add to your list?
questions.why: The screen displayed a search bar prompting for a city, state, or ZIP code to add a new location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact location you need information for.
questions.check: What does the add-city field contain?
questions.say_example: Added <the city> to your list.
